questions.problem: What is the center of the hyperbola $\frac{{y}^{2}}{5}-\frac{(x+7)^{2}}{6}=1?$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

Note that the given equation can be rewritten as follows:

$$
\frac{(y-0)^{2}}{5}-\frac{(x-(-7))^{2}}{6}=1
$$

In this case, we have $h=-7$ and $k=0.$

Therefore, the center of the hyperbola is $(-7,0).$

questions.problem:
What is the center of the hyperbola 
$-2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+12x=22?$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+12x & =22 \\ {y}^{2}-2{x}^{2}+12x & =22 \\ {y}^{2}-2[{x}^{2}-6x] & =22 \\ {y}^{2}-2[(x-3)^{2}-9] & =22 \\ {y}^{2}-2(x-3)^{2}+18 & =22 \\ {y}^{2}-2(x-3)^{2} & =4 \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{4}-\frac{(x-3)^{2}}{2} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center is $(3,0).$

The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-4{y}^{2}-10x-16y & =-5 \\ ({x}^{2}-10x)-4({y}^{2}+4y) & =-5 \\ [(x-5)^{2}-25]-4[(y+2)^{2}-4] & =-5 \\ (x-5)^{2}-25-4(y+2)^{2}+16 & =-5 \\ (x-5)^{2}-4(y+2)^{2} & =-5+25-16 \\ (x-5)^{2}-4(y+2)^{2} & =4 \\ \frac{(x-5)^{2}}{{2}^{2}}-\frac{(y+2)^{2}}{{1}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-5)^{2}}{{2}^{2}}-\frac{(y-(-2))^{2}}{{1}^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center of the hyperbola is $(\,5,-2\,).$

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}+16{y}^{2}-32y-8x & =16 \\ 16{y}^{2}-32y-{x}^{2}-8x & =16 \\ 16[{y}^{2}-2y]-[{x}^{2}+8x] & =16 \\ 16[(y-1)^{2}-1]-[(x+4)^{2}-16] & =16 \\ 16(y-1)^{2}-16-(x+4)^{2}+16 & =16 \\ 16(y-1)^{2}-(x+4)^{2} & =16 \\ \frac{(y-1)^{2}}{1}-\frac{(x+4)^{2}}{16} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-1)^{2}}{1}-\frac{(x-(-4))^{2}}{16} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center of the hyperbola is $(\,-4,1\,).$

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}16{x}^{2}-9{y}^{2}-54y & =-63 \\ 16{x}^{2}-[\,9{y}^{2}+54y\,] & =-63 \\ 16{x}^{2}-[\,9({y}^{2}+6y)\,] & =-63 \\ 16{x}^{2}-[\,9((y+3)^{2}-9)\,] & =-63 \\ 16{x}^{2}-9(y+3)^{2}+81 & =-63 \\ 16{x}^{2}-9(y+3)^{2} & =-63-81 \\ 16{x}^{2}-9(y+3)^{2} & =-144 \\ \frac{(y+3)^{2}}{{4}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{3}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-(-3))^{2}}{{4}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{3}^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
